figures.name: Fig01_sites_and_actual_contact
figures.caption: Left: original specimen, anchors, sampled original precuts and imposed path arrows. Right: actual accepted state and per-node contact forces (at most 18 arrows per source, physical scale shown). No tangential friction law; offset normal loading may produce mixed deformation. Attached points gray; free points colored by exact component ID.

figures.name: Fig02_historical_and_multisite_timing
figures.caption: A/B share sites and trajectories; B source 1 starts 0.4 ms later. The dotted historical single-source path is context, with a different contact position/direction. Equal travel does not imply equal force or work. Dashed vertical line marks the common 2.8 ms cohort, not guaranteed last contact.

figures.name: Fig02b_actual_loading_locations
figures.caption: Actual historical and frozen new external sphere centers and complete inward travel arrows on the same original geometry, physical ROI and camera. A/B sites are identical. Historical geometry is read from its accepted indenter implementation; it is not a same-geometry source-number control.

figures.name: Fig03_failed_network_and_surviving_bridges
figures.caption: Final actual damage/topology on reference geometry for comparable bridge locations. Original bulk/interface identity is retained; all interface failures are displayed separately. The original notch is not counted as naturally failed. Displayed bulk/bridge samples only reduce clutter; all original IDs and full counts remain in the evidence. Black path stays outside |Y| ≤ 50 µm and proves surviving three-dimensional connectivity to anchors. Pinned graph cuts are diagnostics, not fracture energy.

figures.name: Fig03b_damage_nucleation_locations
figures.caption: Birth centroids use actual original bonds of new fully failed bulk networks, excluding precuts. A birth is a discrete failed-edge component event, not a resolved crack surface or a free fragment. Reference geometry is explicitly used.

figures.name: Fig04_simultaneous_evolution
figures.caption: Actual accepted FP64 states, displacement ×1, gray attached body and component-ID colors for detached points. Missing events are explicitly absent. All particles inside the fixed ROI are plotted; out-of-ROI counts are shown. A ≥2-node event can be unresolved debris. All internal live bonds are shown for ≥14-node free components, with no invented shell.

figures.name: Fig04_staggered_evolution
figures.caption: Actual accepted FP64 states, displacement ×1, gray attached body and component-ID colors for detached points. Missing events are explicitly absent. All particles inside the fixed ROI are plotted; out-of-ROI counts are shown. A ≥2-node event can be unresolved debris. All internal live bonds are shown for ≥14-node free components, with no invented shell.

figures.name: Fig05_size_distributions
figures.caption: Six frozen size bins from actual free connected components. Volumes use node count × reference node volume, and equivalent diameters are in CSV/JSON. Bins are exploratory discretization categories, not medical particle classes. Zero bars are retained.

figures.name: Fig05b_independent_objective_constraints
figures.caption: Independent size, mass, dominance and fine-debris metrics; no weighted total masks failure. Undefined fractions before detachment are gaps. Dotted thresholds are frozen exploratory constraints; common cohort time 2.8 ms is dashed.

figures.name: Fig06_fragment_ID_spatial_view
figures.caption: Exact member IDs define free components, colored consistently within each case across the evolution panels. Attached material remains neutral gray. Component IDs are labeled for ≥14-node groups; all component memberships are available in registry and history. Camera clipping is counted, not hidden.

figures.name: Fig06b_full_extent
figures.caption: All final points, without the 3D ROI clipping, in X–Z projection. Colors use exact surviving-component identity; overlap in projection does not merge fragments.

figures.name: Fig07_fragment_birth_split_and_cohesion
figures.caption: Exact original memberships define births and split ancestry. Lifelines are shown for all ≥2-node components; up to five largest have internal-cohesion traces. A two-node pair remains unresolved debris, even with 100% survival. Lifetimes are right-censored by the actual final time; the common 2.8 ms cohort is dashed.

figures.name: Fig08_per_source_force_work_energy
figures.caption: Actual independent native source reactions and independently integrated work. W0+W1 = ΔU + ΔK + D + ΔUc − Jc + ΔUi + R; no damping. R is numerical accounting error, not dissipation. Dashed lines mark each protocol’s scheduled return; recontact remains possible.
